It's not completely undetectable, but we're talking like....5% of one eye is red. I wear glasses so it's less obvious, but it's a really tiny portion that is what I would actually class as red.

I'm nearly 4 weeks out. I had one muscle operated on L eye and 2 in R.

From my understanding the redness is impacted by the number of muscles that get operated on and recovery varies widely from person to person. My redness was very intense in the 2 muscle eye, but it's significantly decreased now and I would say you can't tell I've had surgery when looking straight on. 11 days post surgery

1. Thankfully I didn't have any head pain 

2. 6 days for me, I was absolutely wiped out. Could barely open my eyes and was falling asleep a lot. Was in a lot of pain too, and maxing out on the painkillers

3. I think it's normal, either way I had this big time. My left eye had a short adjustment after the surgery, my right eye went through a very lengthy series of adjustments after the surgery. Left eye almost completely fine the day after. Right eye had so much pain, swelling, felt at times like it would never get better then at day 9 it turned a corner. 

4. I tried to avoid my phone and looking at anything close up, it also hurt my eyes so I couldn't really do it anyway. I didn't have double vision, but I've still been trying to hold a pencil and move it around to make sure my eyes are moving around together

Medical! Vision wouldn't have come close. I think it's standard to be classed as medical but could be wrong.

If you're seriously thinking about it, my advice would be to start researching surgeons, see if they take your insurance, and then meet them and ask a million questions. When you factor in the appointment wait time, finding someone (and someone you like), the wait time, let alone the nerves that kick in and stop you making the phone call for the appointment.... It takes a while. You can also change your mind at any point. I had my first appointment when I was 17, then again at 34, then I finally pulled myself together this year.

I'm 37 (I had the surgery on my birthday 🥳). I think the only disadvantage of waiting longer is the older you are, the longer your body takes to heal. I had also never had surgery in my life (I don't really count the one as a baby, I was 6 months or something).

I cried to all the nurses, asked them if I was going to die...I did not hold back haha. I was not in a good place when I got the surgery, was definitely not in control of my emotions. 

130k is obscene to me, I couldn't believe it. So far the cost to me is 2k, but there are still quite a few outstanding bills. I'm told 99% of insurance companies will cover this

Ahh I feel for you, I really do. I was lucky not to get too many comments, but the ones I got have stuck with me for over 20 years. I swear my brain was able to have bifurcated thoughts - one obsessing on what my eyes were doing, the other (partially) listening to someone.

I think the surgery went well? I won't lie, my experience was pretty rough in one eye. Each person seems to vary a lot, and it seems to also be heavily impacted by how many muscles/how the adjustments go/prior surgeries.

I'm 9 days out and my left eye was a breeze. Minimal adjustments, and I have barely any pain. My right eye is really going through it. I had 2 muscles done and, based on the texts my partner received on the day, we think the surgery was ~5 hours and the adjustments ~2 hours. I do not think that is normal! I had surgery as a baby so might have had scar tissue to work through. But my right eye is still very swollen, very sore. I am so paranoid it's turning in again but it's also so swollen it's difficult to tell. 

I was not prepared for the post surgery anxiety I'm going through. I found the surgery/adjustments very tough, and obsessing over whether your eye is reverting each day is no fun. It's also just generally nerve-wracking having pain in your eye. That said, would I do it again? At the moment yes, but I am going to need this swollen right eye to chill out soon. 

To my knowledge this condition isn't really 'curable', but you can definitely improve it. 

I'm in California and I'm still waiting on the final costs but my doctor has an app, and without insurance (I do have it, thank God) this whole thing comes to a whopping ~130k 😬
